To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dark matter candidate has a gauge coupling comparable to that of a neutralino and that it can be produced in a collider.
the gauge couplings in a dark matter candidate are comparable to those in a neutralino.
the gauge couplings in a multi-component dark matter scenario are comparable to those in a neutralino scenario.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the dark matter candidate, the neutralino.
the study of gauge coupling unification in the context of the minimal supersymmetric extension of the Standard Model.
the gauge coupling of a new dark-matter candidate and its implications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a multicomponent scenario with a new dark matter component can explain all the observed dark matter properties and can provide an explanation for the discrepancy between the observed dark matter density and that predicted by the standard model.
the dark energy is the most mysterious and the most important problem of the present cosmology.
the gauge couplings are a powerful and unique probe to test the existence of dark matter and to discriminate between the different scenarios.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new dark matter scenario which can be tested at the LHC.
a new dark matter particle can be as light as the neutralino and still be compatible with the gauge coupling unification, provided that it couples to the SM particles via a new gauge boson.
the dark matter is a new particle with a mass in the TeV region and a new gauge interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gauge couplings are not a reliable guide to the nature of the dark matter candidate.
the dark matter gauge couplings are not necessarily suppressed, as is often assumed in the literature.
a multicomponent DM scenario can be realized in a simple extension of the Standard Model.
